app.title: Console
nav.label: Sections
login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Enter the console token. It is KODRA_CONSOLE_TOKEN in the agent's .env file, or in its Kubernetes Secret.
login.tooMany: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
login.passwordIntro: Sign in with your console username and password. The first time, use admin and admin; you will set a new password right away.
login.wrongPassword: That username or password is not right.
login.useToken: Sign in with a token instead
login.usePassword: Sign in with a username and password
password.title: Change the admin password
password.intro: The admin is signed out everywhere else once it changes.
password.rules: At least 12 characters, and not the current password.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.wrong-current: The current password is not right.
password.weak: Use at least 12 characters, different from the current password.
password.too-many: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
password.failed: The password was not saved. Try again.
overview.title: Overview
connectors.title: Connectors
activity.title: Activity
activity.intro: Everything the agent did, from its audit log. Secrets are removed.
investigations.title: Investigations
investigations.intro: Alerts the agent looked into, read-only, and what it found.
usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: Tokens the agent used, from its audit log.
usage.priceSource: Cost is estimated from {source} list prices as of {date}.
usage.priceOverride: Cost is estimated from the prices in kodra-agent.yaml.
usage.noPrice: No price is known for {model}. Set spec.console.pricing in kodra-agent.yaml to see an estimated cost.
usage.cacheRate: {rate} of input tokens came from the cache.
usage.question: Question
approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.intro: Changes the agent asked for, and what an approver decided, here or in Slack.
connectors.usedByShip: Used by kodra-agent ship to build and test images. The model gets no tools from it.
connectors.usedForChat: Used for Slack messages and approvals. The model gets no tools from it.
chat.title: Chat
chat.queued: Waiting for a free slot. At most 2 questions run at once.
chat.offline: Lost the connection to the agent. Trying again.
chat.start: Ask a question below to start.
approval.confirm: Run {action} now? This changes your system.
approval.cannot: Waiting for an approver. Sign in with a console approver token to decide here.
approval.expired: This request expired. Nothing was run.
approval.counted: Your approval is counted. It needs another approver.
approval.refused.self: You asked for this change, so someone else must approve it.
approval.refused.not-listed: You are not an approver for this change.
approval.refused.already-approved: You already approved this. It needs another approver.
chat.policy: Reads run on their own. Changes wait for an approver.
chat.placeholderBusy: You can write your next message while it works
chat.stopHint: Stop ends this answer and keeps what it found so far. Nothing it was about to change runs.
chat.hint: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line. Up to {n} characters.
chat.emptyIntro: I can read {connectors}. I ask an approver before I change anything.
chat.suggest.source: Which merge requests or pull requests are open?
chat.suggest.cicd: Did the last pipeline fail, and why?
chat.suggest.cloud: Are any alarms firing right now?
chat.suggest.monitoring: Which alerts are firing right now?
approval.runsExactly: Runs these steps exactly, and stops if a file changed since this preview.
pause.pausedBy: Paused by {who} at {time}. Reads and chat keep working; nothing is changed until an approver resumes.
overview.runningText: Reads run on their own. Changes wait for an approver. Pausing refuses every change until you resume; reads and chat keep working.
overview.review: Review them on the Approvals page.
overview.budgetShare: {share}% of the budget. Questions stop at 100%.
overview.budgetOver: The budget is used up. New questions are refused; alerts are still investigated.
overview.noBudget: No monthly budget set. An estimate from list prices.
settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: What the agent can reach, who approves its changes, and its limits.
settings.kubernetes: Settings are read-only here: the chart's console.editSettings is off. Change values.yaml and run helm upgrade, or turn console.editSettings on.
settings.viewOnly: You can look, but only a console approver can change settings.
settings.undoConfirm: Put the previous settings back and restart?
settings.moreIntro: These work but are less tested, and may change. Each one stays off until you turn it on.
settings.connector.tools: Tools the agent gets: {read} read, {write} write
settings.connector.toolsLater: Each tool, its risk, and its limits show here once the connector runs.
settings.secret.hint: It is checked first, then saved in .env on this machine. It is never shown again.
settings.policy.approversHint: Slack handles like @omar, Slack user ids, or console approvers like console:omar. Each console approver gets their own sign-in token.
settings.policy.expiry: Minutes an approval request stays open
settings.policy.denyHint: Deleting, wiping, or changing things that cannot be undone is never possible. The safe default.
settings.policy.require-approvalHint: An approver can allow a destructive action, one at a time.
settings.limits.tokenBudgetHint: Weighted by price: tokens read from the cache count a tenth.
settings.limits.budgetLabel: Budget per month, in US dollars
settings.limits.budgetHint: Leave it empty for no budget. When it is used up, new questions are refused; alerts are still investigated.
settings.console.title: Console
settings.console.chatHint: Ask the agent questions here. Changes still wait for an approver.
settings.console.offHint: The console cannot turn itself off. To turn it off, change kodra-agent.yaml on the host.
settings.network.title: Trusted certificates
settings.network.intro: Extra CA certificates the agent and its connectors trust, besides the usual public ones: an internal CA, a proxy that inspects TLS, or Amazon RDS (download its global-bundle.pem from https://truststore.pki.rds.amazonaws.com/global/global-bundle.pem).
settings.network.chart: On Kubernetes, set caBundle in the chart's values.
settings.network.hint: Certificates only, never a private key. They are saved in the bundle folder under ca/, and the agent restarts to use them.
settings.confirm: Save and restart the agent now?
settings.saveHint: The agent restarts to apply this, in about 15 seconds. The current file is kept, and Undo last change puts it back. The change is in the audit log with your name.
settings.restartingText: It applies the new settings and comes back in about 15 seconds. You stay signed in.
settings.stale: The settings changed while you were editing. Review them again.
settings.notBack: The agent did not come back in time. Check that it is running: docker compose ps.
settings.more.title: More access
settings.more.write: {connector} can propose changes, each after an approval.
settings.more.destructive: Destructive actions are allowed with approval.
settings.more.chat: Anyone signed in can chat with the agent.
people.kubernetes: Sign-in tokens are read-only here. On Kubernetes, the agent needs the chart's console.editSettings and an existingSecret to change them.
people.accountsIntro: The shared token lets your team look and chat. Each console approver has their own token and can approve changes.
people.rotateConfirm: The old token stops working when the agent restarts.
people.rotateConfirmSelf: This is your token: you will sign in again with the new one.
people.removeConfirm: They can no longer sign in or approve here.
people.addHint: Lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. They get their own token, shown once.
people.tokenOnce: Copy it now and send it to them privately. It is shown only once, and the agent keeps it only in .env.
people.restarting: The agent is restarting to use the change.
people.back: The agent is back. The new token works now.
people.signInAgain: The agent is back. Your token changed, so sign in with the new one.
people.sessionsIntro: Browsers that used the console since the agent last started.
people.noSessions: Nobody else has used the console since the agent started.
settings.kubernetesSaved: Settings saved here live in the agent's ConfigMap. Before a helm upgrade with a changed config, start from that copy (see the chart notes).
approval.frozen: {environment} is frozen ({name}, until {until} {timezone}). Approving overrides the freeze, and every approver is told.
approval.refused.change-ref-missing: Approving this needs a change reference.
approval.refused.change-ref-format: The change reference does not have the required format.
approval.refused.reason-missing: This environment is frozen. Approving needs a reason for the override.
settings.held: Saved for review: this policy change waits for a second approver, and applies once they approve it.
settings.policyHeld: This changes who may change what. It waits for a second approver before it applies.
settings.policyAnnounced: This changes who may change what. Every approver is told, with this diff.
people.held: This change waits for a second approver. Once it is approved, create the new approver's token with Rotate.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: What the agent can see in your tools right now. Read only, refreshed at most once a minute.
dashboard.none: None of the connected tools has a dashboard yet. Kubernetes, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, and Jenkins do.
dashboard.noTargets: Nothing is listed for this connector yet. Add namespaces, projects, or repos in Settings.
dashboard.unavailable: Not available: the connector is not running, or its server does not offer this.
dashboard.pods.allGood: Every pod is running, with no restarts.
model.intro: Models your {provider} key can use, with list prices per million tokens. The cost is this month's questions priced at each model.
model.listError: The provider's list could not be read ({error}), so these are the models Kodra knows.
model.saveNote: Saving tries the new model with one tiny call first, then restarts the agent on it.
provider.title: Switch to another model provider
provider.keySetHint: This key is already in .env. Leave the field empty to use it, or paste a new one.
provider.notWritable: Keys cannot be saved here. On Kubernetes, the chart needs console.editSettings and an existingSecret.
provider.warnTitle: From now on, questions, logs, and tool output go to {provider}.
provider.switchNote: The agent asks the model one tiny question with the new key first, then saves the key to .env, keeps the old one, and restarts. Undo last change puts the old provider back.
settings.more.model: Questions, logs, and tool output go to {to} instead of {from}.
context.warning: {model} runs with {window} tokens of context, and this agent needs about {needed} for its instructions and tools. Ollama cuts off the start of a longer prompt, so answers would be wrong. Set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH to 65536 where Ollama runs and restart Ollama, or turn off connectors you do not need.
dashboard.jobs.none: None of the listed jobs were found.
welcome.more: And {n} more on the other pages.
welcome.paused: Changes are paused by {who}. Reads and chat still work.
welcome.approvals.one: {n} approval is waiting for a decision
welcome.approvals.other: {n} approvals are waiting for a decision
welcome.budgetOver: The monthly budget is used up, so new questions are refused
welcome.budgetNear: {share}% of this month's budget is used
welcome.runsFailed.one: {n} recent pipeline run or job failed
welcome.runsFailed.other: {n} recent pipeline runs or jobs failed
welcome.briefingPrompt: Give me a briefing on what is going on: anything failing, waiting, or unusual across the connected tools, and what you would look at first.
welcome.sys.unreadable: Some cards could not be read
settings.entries.name: Name
settings.entries.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, like orders-replica.
checks.title: Daily checks
checks.noSchedule: No schedule set. Add one under spec.checks in kodra-agent.yaml, or run the checks now.
checks.never: The checks have not run yet.
checks.notChecked: Not checked (connector off or nothing listed): {list}.
checks.runFailed: The checks could not run. Try again in a minute.
checks.askPrompt: The daily checks found this in {where}: {title}. What is the likely cause, and what would you check first?
settings.secret.readOnly: Secrets cannot be changed here. Set them where the agent runs.
settings.secret.fileHint: It is checked and tested first, then saved as a file only the agent can read, in the bundle folder (or in the agent’s Secret on Kubernetes). It is never shown again.
settings.secret.paste.ssh-private-key: Paste the private key here (-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- …)
settings.connector.missing: Still needed before this connector works:
settings.connector.missingHint: Each one is under Secrets below, with the steps to get it.
setup.copyFailed: Select the text and copy it.
repos.title: Repos
repos.intro: Onboard a repo: what it needs and its risks, then a pull request with its Dockerfile, CI, Helm chart, and the report.
repos.none: No repos yet. Add GitHub repos or GitLab projects to their connector, and they show up here.
repos.previewNote: Onboarding uses the ship flow, which is in preview: it works but is less tested, and may change.
repos.how: Analyze reads the repo and writes the report, without running anything in it, and posts the risks and questions to Slack. Open pull request adds what is missing and waits for an approval in Approvals before it pushes. The agent has no Docker access, so the pull request's CI builds the image.
repos.approverOnly: Only a console approver can onboard a repo.
repos.readOnly: Its connector is read-only, so it can be analyzed but not given a pull request. Give it read-write-approved access in Settings, Connectors.
repos.waiting: It asks for an approval before it pushes.
settings.more.broad: {connector} keeps a credential with more access than it needs.
settings.more.namedModel: Data from an environment can go to the model {name}.
settings.more.tracing: Traces (names and durations, no content) go to {endpoint}.
more.profile.title: Profile
more.profile.starterHint: One approver is enough, and they may approve their own requests.
more.profile.teamHint: Nobody approves their own request; production needs two approvers; policy changes are announced.
more.profile.strictHint: Two approvers, change references in production, and policy changes wait for a second approver.
more.rules.intro: The profile decides these unless you set them here.
more.rules.selfApproval: The person who asked may approve
more.rules.selfApprovalHint: Off: someone else has to approve each change.
more.rules.changeRefHint: Like a ticket number, written to the audit log. Nothing calls a ticketing system.
more.env.intro: Environments group namespaces and repos with their own approvers, rules, and freezes. A change covers one environment.
more.env.name: Name
more.freeze.title: Freezes
more.freeze.intro: During a freeze, a write needs an approver to override it, with a reason.
more.freeze.name: Name
more.checks.title: Scheduled checks
more.checks.intro: Read-only checks that post a digest of what is new, still broken, and fixed.
more.checks.name: Name
more.checks.quiet: Post nothing when every check is clean
more.checks.quietHint: The digest is still saved and shown here.
more.monitoring.title: Alert investigations
more.monitoring.intro: Limits on how many alerts the agent looks into, so a storm of alerts cannot run up the bill.
more.monitoring.cooldown: Minutes before the same alert is looked into again
more.writes.title: Changes per hour
more.writes.label: Approved writes per hour
more.writes.hint: Across Slack, the console, and alerts. Past it, writes are refused until the hour has room again.
more.models.title: Other models
more.models.intro: Named models an environment can keep its data to, like a local model for production.
more.models.name: Name
more.proxy.title: Proxy
more.proxy.intro: Every outbound connection goes through it. The URLs are kept as secrets, since they can hold a password.
more.mirrors.title: Base image mirrors
more.mirrors.intro: Ship pulls base images from these mirrors instead, for networks without Docker Hub.
more.privacy.title: Masked before the model sees it
more.privacy.intro: Customer data the agent masks in tool output, logs, and questions, besides secrets.
more.patterns.title: Your own patterns
more.patterns.intro: Regular expressions for data of your own to mask, like order or customer ids.
more.patterns.name: Name
more.obs.title: Observability
more.obs.metricsHint: Counts and durations on their own port, never content.
more.obs.tracingHint: Names and durations of turns, model calls, and tool calls; no content.
more.obs.stdoutHint: Each audit record, already redacted, as a JSON line for a log collector.
more.broad.label: Keep a credential with more access than the agent needs
more.broad.hint: Off: a cluster-admin kubeconfig, or one that reads Secrets, is refused. On: it is kept, and the agent warns at every start.
more.health.doctorIntro: Every check doctor runs: the config, each secret and connector, the network, and the audit log.
more.health.auditIntro: Checks that no audit record was changed or removed since it was written.
